title: MEPC 84 summary report
key_claim: MEPC 84 did not adopt the Net-Zero Framework because members could not compromise between adopting the draft with minimal change and a market-readiness approach; MEPC 85 is tentatively scheduled for 30 November to 3 December, with MEPC ES.2 planned to resume for one day on Friday 4 December.
frame_summary: Lloyd's Register reads MEPC 84 as deferral rather than failure: the framework text survives unchanged and the adoption decision has been compressed into a dated December window that owners should plan against.

title: Shipping's transition being hampered by policy uncertainty, yet industry progress continues
key_claim: The fifth UCL Energy Institute and Getting to Zero Coalition progress review finds zero-emission-fuel-capable vessels fell from 9.5% to 5.7% of total tonnage on order, and recommends the IMO adopt the Net-Zero Framework unchanged in December to restore policy clarity.
frame_summary: The Global Maritime Forum and UCL argue the transition is stalling for want of policy, not technology: the failure to adopt the framework is the single most transition-regressive event in five years and adoption in December would let acceleration begin in earnest.
verbatim_quote: Adoption of the Net-Zero Framework at the IMO would allow that acceleration to begin in earnest.

single most transition-regressive event we've seen in the five years this report has been running

title: Fuel Switch Snapshot: Pooling slump erodes LBM's compliance edge
key_claim: ENGINE's assessed FuelEU pooling value fell EUR 21.70/mtCO2e in a week to EUR 86.90/mtCO2e, with OceanScore reporting some surplus deals closing below the cost of generating the surplus, a sign of market overshooting.
frame_summary: ENGINE, a bunker-market data provider, reads the pooling slump as a functioning but oversupplied compliance market in which falling surplus prices are eroding the economics of premium low-carbon fuels such as liquefied biomethane.

title: Alternative-fuelled ship orders outpace 2025, led by LNG with an 'old' new fuel emerging
key_claim: DNV Alternative Fuels Insight data show 69 alternative fuel-capable vessels ordered in September 2026 (48 LNG, 9 LPG, 12 ethanol bulk carriers, none ammonia or hydrogen), with 2026 orders 53% higher than at the same point in 2025 and 200 of them LNG, up 52% year-on-year.
frame_summary: Riviera reads the ordering data as owners converging on LNG and even reviving ethanol, with FuelEU directing attention to well-to-wake reductions, while zero-emission fuels sit out the order surge.

title: FuelEU Maritime Pooling 2026: Why Have Prices Fallen and What Lies Ahead for Shipping Companies?
key_claim: FuelEU pooled-surplus prices fell from EUR 213.00/tCO2e in January 2026 to EUR 118.90/tCO2e by 24 August 2026, approximately 44.2% lower, in a first compliance year in which more than 12,000 compliance balance reports were verified by 30 April and the pooling mechanism was used by 90% of vessels.
frame_summary: EUCMX, a carbon-trading platform, argues the price fall reflects a maturing, transparent and oversupplied surplus market rather than a failing one, with banking and the unchanged 2% target keeping demand soft until 2029.
verbatim_quote: Compared with the January 2026 level of EUR 213/tCO2e, the August 2026 price was approximately 44.2% lower.
verbatim_list: January 2026 – 2025 surplus: EUR 213.00/tCO2e
24 August 2026: EUR 118.90/tCO2e
By 30 April, more than 12,000 compliance balance reports had been successfully verified, covering over 90% of vessels.
EMSA also reported that the pooling mechanism was used by 90% of vessels.
notes: EUCMX is a commercial carbon-trading platform, so classified Tier 4 and treated directionally; its January and August figures are OceanScore OPX prices and its verification figures are attributed to EMSA.
